attempted_claim: Let K≥1 be fixed. For every sequence of finite sets B⊂ℤ with |B|→∞, and every A⊆B·B satisfying |A+A|≤K|A|, must |A|=o(|B|²)? Equivalently, must E⁺(B·B)=o(|B|⁶) hold for every finite integer set B, without any bound on the magnitudes of its elements?
decisive_failure: No unconditional proof and no fixed-K counterexample were obtained. All proof routes in reach require a polynomial bound on element magnitudes; bounded small-set scans and the prime-interval artifact rows (density 0.25 with doubling growing 5.28 to 9.82) produced no fixed-K refutation. Work was further limited by a stream disconnect and the expired budget, which forbade new avenues, long computations, and literature search.
